Buses on a route arrive with irregular gaps that average 10 minutes apart (sometimes 2 minutes, sometimes 18). If you arrive at the bus stop at a uniformly random time, is your average wait longer than, shorter than, or equal to 5 minutes (half the average gap)?

questions.q: During WWII, statistician Abraham Wald examined returning bomber planes and found bullet holes concentrated on the wings and tail, with far fewer on the engines. Where did he recommend adding armor?
choices: The wings and tail, since that's where the most hits were observed
The engines — the area with no hits, because planes hit there usually didn't return
Nowhere — no extra armor was needed

questions.q: A player has a higher batting average than another player in both the first half and the second half of a season. Is it possible for the first player to still have the LOWER batting average for the season overall?
choices: No — if one player is better in both halves, they must be better overall
Yes — if they had very different numbers of at-bats in each half, this reversal (Simpson's paradox) can occur
No, this situation is mathematically impossible for any two players
Only if both players had exactly the same number of at-bats

questions.q: Hilbert's Grand Hotel has infinitely many rooms, all of them occupied. A single new guest arrives and asks for a room. Can the hotel accommodate them without evicting anyone?
choices: Yes — move the guest in room n to room n+1 for every n, which frees up room 1
No — a fully occupied infinite hotel has no space for anyone else
Only if the new guest is willing to share a room
Only if an existing guest checks out first

questions.q: In the Monty Hall problem, after the host opens a losing door, should you switch?
choices: No — the first pick keeps its advantage
Only if the host chose randomly
